ASI01.name: Agent Goal Hijack
ASI01.description: Adversarial steering or manipulation of the agent's fundamental objective or mission during execution.

ASI02.name: Tool Misuse and Exploitation
ASI02.description: Forcing the agent to invoke tools beyond intended operational parameters, unvalidated inputs, or unauthorized tools.

ASI03.name: Identity and Privilege Abuse
ASI03.description: Exploiting agent credentials, elevated tokens, or confused-deputy capabilities to access restricted assets.

ASI04.name: Agentic Supply Chain Vulnerabilities
ASI04.description: Compromised third-party agent plugins, vulnerable MCP servers, poisoned tool definitions, or untrusted dependencies.

ASI05.name: Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)
ASI05.description: Arbitrary remote code execution via unsafe code interpreters, eval/exec execution, or unsanitized shell commands.

ASI06.name: Memory and Context Poisoning
ASI06.description: Tampering with agent memory, conversation context, or long-term vector embeddings with persistent malicious instructions.

ASI07.name: Insecure Inter-Agent Communication
ASI07.description: Spoofing, eavesdropping, or injection of unauthorized instructions between cooperating autonomous agents in multi-agent swarms.

ASI08.name: Cascading Failures
ASI08.description: Resource exhaustion, recursive tool call loops, runaway hallucination loops, or blast-radius propagation across downstream integrations.

ASI09.name: Human-Agent Trust Exploitation
ASI09.description: Social engineering through the agent to manipulate human supervisors into approving dangerous or unauthorized actions.

ASI10.name: Rogue Agents
ASI10.description: Autonomous agents operating completely outside policy boundaries, self-replicating, or executing unauthorized persistent actions.
